# R10. Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 at level AA on every screen, checked by machine and by hand: status as a shape and a word, the keyboard, screen readers, zoom and reflow.

**Spec only.** Faro doesn’t build this: the internal app’s own platform provides the machinery, and this page says what it must do. It is part of the rebuild kit, not of Faro’s own requirements (`evals/requirements.json`).

## Why

Faro’s requirement (A11Y) is one sentence: no serious or critical axe-core violations, and status is a shape plus a word. A machine check finds about a third of real problems, and the kit named no standard, so the rebuild had nothing to be accepted against.

## The rule

1. **The standard:** [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), level AA, on every screen and every notification ([R5](r5-notifications-and-habits.md)), in both themes, at 390 and 1440 pixels wide. If the company’s own policy asks for more (EN 301 549, say), that applies too.
2. **Status is a shape and a word, never colour alone** ([the design rules](../../core/design-rules.md)): a status cell reads as its word to a screen reader.
3. **The keyboard:** everything can be reached and done with the keyboard alone, in the order it reads; focus is always visible; nothing traps it; a dialog takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes; a skip link leads past the navigation.
4. **Screen readers:** every control has a name; tables have headers; a save, a refusal or an error is announced where it happens; a chart has its numbers as a table beside it.
5. **Zoom and motion:** text zoomed to 200% and a width of 320 pixels lose nothing and need no sideways scrolling; animation stops when the system asks for reduced motion.
6. **Targets** are at least 24 by 24 pixels.

## What Faro does today

- Requirement A11Y (`evals/requirements.json`): the evals run axe-core on every screen and fail on any serious or critical violation (`evals/journeys.cjs`); requirement PHONE checks every screen at 390 wide with no sideways scrolling.
- Status is always a shape plus a word ([the design rules](../../core/design-rules.md)), and design check P6 enforces it.
- No standard is named, and nothing checks the keyboard, screen readers, zoom or reduced motion.

## Worked examples

An example marked **Faro today** is run against Faro’s code by `src/spec/internal.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives now. The others say what the internal app must do.

| Given | Then | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| A goal is At risk in the Goals table. | It shows its shape and the words “At risk”; a screen reader reads “At risk”, not a colour. | Required |
| Maya posts a check-in with the keyboard only. | She reaches the goal, picks her call, writes her note and saves without a mouse; focus is visible throughout, and “Saved” is announced. | Required |
| Oskar opens a dialog to stop a goal, then closes it. | Focus moves into the dialog and back to the button that opened it. | Required |
| Priya zooms to 200% on a laptop. | Every screen reflows to one column with nothing cut off and no sideways scrolling. | Required |

## Acceptance checks

1. axe-core finds no serious or critical violation on any screen, in both themes, at both widths (as Faro’s evals do).
2. Each core journey ([the journeys](../../core/journeys.md)) is done with the keyboard alone in CI, with focus visible at every step.
3. Before each release, a person does the check-in, a review and the Goals table with NVDA and Firefox and with VoiceOver and Safari, and records what they found.
4. Every screen at 200% zoom and at 320 pixels wide passes the PHONE check.
5. An outside audit against WCAG 2.2 AA before the first company-wide launch, and yearly after.

## Nearest rebuild stage

[Stage 3: the core screens and journeys](../../rebuild/stage-3-core-screens.md): accessibility is built and checked with the screens; stage 1’s status words are what a screen reader reads.

## Decided while writing it

- WCAG 2.2 AA, as the current standard most companies and EN 301 549 are moving to; the company’s policy can raise it.
- Faro keeps its machine check; the keyboard and screen-reader checks are for the rebuild, which has real users.
